title: Return to Hana’s Tower
dek: A missing host brings the company back to the tower. The rescue becomes a fatal fight, followed by damaged mechanisms, erased writing and murals that leave more to investigate.

facts.Recorded dates: 27–29 Oct 2026 · quest source posts; one continuing expedition
facts.Setting: Petal Market; Hana’s tower; Larkhollow; Verdelune
facts.People: Ryvyt; Pelegia (Pin); Saelihn; Oya; Fenwick; Hana; Talla Briarwing; Ilyra Bellflower
facts.Outcome: Hana dies; Ryvyt and Pin investigate higher floors; the final painting and proposed burial remain unresolved

body:
The company returned to Larkhollow intending to understand its tower. News of Hana’s disappearance turned the visit into a rescue attempt. The friend Ryvyt wanted to protect became the larger figure they fought inside.

The battle ended with Hana dead. Ryvyt and Pelegia, known here as Pin, continued through the tower while its purpose, her nature and Minerva’s situation remained unresolved.

A dress before the rescue

The road to Larkhollow was quiet this time. No dark path opened and no likeness of Viota stopped the travelers. In the Petal Market, flowers, herbs and familiar stalls gave them room to look around. Saelihn admired a blue dress. Oya wanted the Blossom Gown and a suitable occasion to wear it. Ryvyt asked Talla Briarwing whether she had a little flying carpet.

Talla answered that most people here had wings. Her carpets did have another use: she touched one and it became a cloak, changing its style before the visitors. Clothing and conversation went together. When she asked whether they had come because Lady Hana had not been seen, the shopping stopped being the only business at the stall.

Talla wanted purchases before sharing more. Saelihn bought the blue dress, and Oya chose her gown. Talla said Hana had disappeared after people investigated the old tower. Some residents suspected an attack by someone from Larkhollow, but she doubted it because their memories were too foggy. That was her account of the disappearance, not an established culprit.

Ilyra Bellflower supplied a more specific report: a doll resembling Ryvyt had been found at Hana’s tree, along with blood and a message in Sylvan asking someone to come. Ryvyt recognized the doll as part of a gift he had made for Hana. He had stayed in her home on earlier visits. His urgency came from a friendship the others did not all share.

Warnings about another absent friend

The company set out to find Hana. Ryvyt led, with Fenwick offering reassurance. A childlike mental presence asked them not to come. A fast-moving Tik drew them toward the tower, and another figure appeared with a different warning: the Children of Viota claimed to have Minerva captive.

Ryvyt recalled that Minerva had gone with them willingly in exchange for the body the earlier company sought. Pin said she had been promised a way back. Fenwick reported a Sending in which Minerva had said she was safe and in a city. The childlike figures now threatened trouble if the party continued, without letting Saelihn obtain a clear answer about whether Minerva could leave.

Those accounts did not resolve her situation. The company had an earlier self-report relayed by Fenwick and new threats from figures whose purpose was unclear. They continued toward Hana rather than treating the warning as proof that both missing people were in the same place.

As the tower came into view, the trees darkened. Hana’s voice gave a final warning to turn back. Ryvyt believed knowledge was being protected inside. He still wanted to know enough to help.

The guard at the half-open door

A Tik came forward and threw a dagger at Ryvyt. Oya moved to protect him, striking and stunning it. Fenwick used enhanced sight to spot two silent childlike figures near Pin that the others had not seen. He tried to draw them into conversation instead of starting another indiscriminate attack.

Fenwick explained his hesitation: the earlier use of meteors against childlike ghosts still gave him nightmares. Saelihn did not like fighting either, though she could not see how to stop the spirits by talking. Her first psionic attack missed.

Hana’s voice changed as they tried to reach her. At one moment it sounded like the child Ryvyt remembered; at another it became something more psychic. She said a mother had forbidden the tower and invited them to fight. The speaker’s statement did not identify that mother or explain the change in voice.

The Tik’s ticking stopped as a watch broke, and it fell. Oya hoped she had avoided killing it, while noting that it looked constructed. The tower door stood half open. Saelihn wondered whether the child they meant to rescue was a child at all. Ryvyt went in first with his shield ready and insisted the others stay behind him.

The friend they had come to save

Inside, the large figure was identified as Hana. Ryvyt asked why his wooden gift had been found beside blood. The answer came as an attack: a mental force lifted Oya and Pin into the air. Saelihn warped the space holding them and brought both down out of its grasp.

Fenwick tried to clear the surrounding threats with Banishment. He wanted Ryvyt free to deal with Hana and hoped to avoid repeating the destruction of the previous visit. Maintaining that spell made him vulnerable as enemies focused on him. Saelihn formed a psychic image to shield him from a heavy blow.

Ryvyt asked Oya’s trust before speeding her movements with magic. Saelihn drove threats away with one attack, then failed when she tried to strike harder at Hana’s mind. The larger figure rushed her, saying that if it could not escape, no one would. Claws wounded her and held her near its hair.

Ryvyt healed and hurled fire at Hana while asking forgiveness. The figure burned and produced a child’s scream, warning that the memory would haunt him. Saelihn called the cries false, but that was her judgment of what they faced. The scene did not give the company a complete explanation of Hana’s nature before they had to fight her.

A death and an unfinished promise

The resumed narration confirms that Hana died in the tower. Pin’s shadow had struck during the final exchange; the source does not separately award a final blow. When Ryvyt looked at the body, the burned face and hair made the death difficult to distance from the friend he remembered.

He apologized to her and blamed himself. Pin put a hand on his shoulder, saying they had tried not to fight. Ryvyt wanted to bury Hana after they finished, and Pin offered to help. That intention is where the burial stands in this record. No completed funeral is shown.

The earlier doll, the changing voices and the relationship between Hana’s manifestations remained unexplained. The new outcome is nevertheless definite: the narrator identifies Hana’s death in this fight. The uncertainty about her identity must not be used to erase the death that the company now has to live with.

Stairs led both upward and down. Ryvyt and Pin went below, looking for what had been worth guarding. Ryvyt checked for traps and used his tracking lantern when the darkness became difficult.

A workshop without its missing piece

At the bottom lay a damaged Tick with parts missing. Ryvyt could replace ordinary gears and bolts from his supplies, but a special metal component belonged to a clock mechanism he did not recognize. He could not complete the repair. Pin hoped a new companion might also have information to share, if they could get it working.

A narrow gap in the masonry led farther in. They found a small table and a damaged inscription beginning with words about root and stone forgetting. Ryvyt tried Mending. The narrator distinguished repairing a fissure from recovering words deliberately chiseled away: he would need to know the missing text to restore it.

The table held nearly erased signs of roots, a river, towers and a circle. Ryvyt compared them with his map, but found no place showing all of them. The map’s gaps prevented that failure from proving there was no such place.

Pin opened a compartment beneath the table. Its tools, clocks and metal scraps did not contain the component Ryvyt needed. A strange small tool had buttons and a hammerlike part. It did not react when brought near the Tick. Ryvyt thought study might reveal more uses, but the object was not identified or demonstrated as an all-purpose repair solution.

Remember, preserve, endure

Above the entrance floor, painted leaves led them toward a large mural. Some figures appeared similar across its seasons. Ryvyt could not identify them, and the narrator would not confirm the resemblance as recognition of a particular person.

The fragments they could recover included remembering, preserving, enduring and returning. Ryvyt joined them to the words found below. Pin wondered about living trees, Adelia and people caught in other lands. Those comparisons were their attempts to understand the art, not a solved account of the tower’s history.

They decided the material should be recorded and shared for later study. Ryvyt said he was logging it in his memories. Making perfect illusions of the images remained a proposed way to preserve them; the text does not show that work being completed.

The last floor remains a question

The next mural was named the Pilgrims of the Lanterns. Featureless travelers, children and animals carried lights through changing landscapes. Some put their lanterns out, and birds, flowers and stars rose from those flames. Other travelers emerged with familiar colors in new lights, beneath birds circling like a wheel.

Ryvyt read a possible cycle of birth, life, return and rebirth in the procession. Pin thought that might be right. The mural supports that interpretation being considered; it does not establish a universal rule for the lives or returns of Larkhollow’s people.

They climbed again and reached the last floor. There was no ceiling, and the moonlight looked green. The painting before them was named the Gardener Beneath the Moon. The narrator stopped on that image.

Hana’s death is the completed outcome of the return fight. The missing mechanism, damaged words, seasonal figures and final painting are still under investigation at the packet’s cutoff. No identity for the painted Gardener, complete translation, finished Tick repair or burial is supplied by the ending.

People, places and connected histories Larkhollow · Hana · Ryvyt · Pin · Saelihn · Fenwick · Minerva
